title: Yusuf in one sitting, part one
hookLine: Surah 12:1–57, from the dream to the treasury
tomorrow: the brothers walk in, hungry, and don't know him. what will he do?

cards: One final down, more to come. Jordan is on Amira's floor eating chips when she sees what Amira's reading for her nightly page: Surah Yusuf. "Yusuf, like your dad?"
Then she reads a line and sits up. "Wait. Dreams, jealous brothers, a pit, Egypt? That's Joseph. Joseph with the coat. He's in the Qur'an too?" Jordan grew up with him in Sunday school.
Amira grew up with him at Dadi's knee. Same boy, two tellings.

teach.b: Surah Yusuf calls itself, in Pickthall's words, "the best of narratives," and it's told whole, in one surah. Part one runs like this. Yusuf dreams that eleven stars, the sun and the moon bow down to him.
His father Ya'qub tells him: don't tell your brothers, or they'll plot against you. They plot anyway.

teach.h: THE WELL, THE SHIRT, THE PRISON.
teach.b: They drop him into a well, and bring home his shirt with false blood on it. Ya'qub answers with words Dadi still says: "comely patience."
Yusuf is sold into Egypt, resists the temptation of his master's wife, is proven innocent by a shirt torn from behind, and is jailed anyway.
In prison he reads dreams, until the king's dream sets him over the storehouses of the land.

teach.h: HE TOLD IT TO HIS BRETHREN.
teach.b: Now Jordan's telling, Genesis, in the 1917 Jewish translation: "And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brethren; and they hated him yet the more."
Shared: the dreams, the jealous brothers, the pit, Egypt, the rise. The Torah, the Christian Bible and the Qur'an all carry this boy. And the honest difference: in Genesis, Joseph tells his brothers.
In the Qur'an, his father says don't.
Genesis gives him a coat of many colors; the Qur'an gives him a shirt that turns up again and again. That's the line to tell a friend tonight. Neither telling needs the other to be wrong.

how: Muslims read Surah Yusuf whole as a single story; parents and grandparents often tell it to children, and 'comely patience', sabrun jamil, is said in hard times.

games.q: what does “yusuf in one sitting” mean?
o: Surah Yusuf, read whole as one story
a fast Muslims keep in memory of Yusuf
a summary of the Joseph chapters of Genesis

games.q: part one of the story — tap the pairs.
p: stars, sun and moon bow down

s: the Qur'an's Yusuf wears a coat of many colors
the coat is Genesis. the Qur'an tells of his shirt: the false blood, the tear from behind.
Surah Yusuf calls itself the best of narratives
"We narrate unto thee (Muhammad) the best of narratives."

games.q: your little cousin hears part one and asks: 'why did Ya'qub tell Yusuf to keep his dream a secret?' what does the surah say?
o: he feared the brothers would plot against him if they heard it.
dreams were not allowed to be talked about in their family.
Ya'qub didn't believe the dream and didn't want it spread.
games.why: Ya'qub tells him not to tell his brothers, lest they plot against him. they plot anyway.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one person you've envied lately, even a little. Hold their face for the sit and, instead of measuring yourself against them, quietly wish them one good thing.
Jealousy started this whole story; let it stop with you.

wordCard.voice: Yusuf in one sitting: the surah told whole, from the dream to the storehouses, and on to the end tomorrow.

orig.note: Arabic: the best of narratives, the surah's own phrase in 12:3.

carryVoice: To hold onto: the best of stories, carried by more than one people. Halfway through Yusuf.
